import java.io.*;
import java.util.*;

public class I {
    
    public static boolean DEBUG = true;
    public static String name = "I";

    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
        FastScanner scan;
        PrintWriter out;
        if (DEBUG) {
            scan = new FastScanner(System.in);
            out = new PrintWriter(System.out);
        } else {
            scan = new FastScanner(name + ".in");
            out = new PrintWriter(new BufferedWriter(new FileWriter(name + ".out")));
        }

        int N = Integer.parseInt(scan.nextString());
        double P = Double.parseDouble(scan.nextString());
        
        // Edge case: if P is 0, answer is 0
        if (P <= 0) {
            out.println(0);
            out.close();
            return;
        }
        
        // Try different number of maps to study (i)
        for (int i = 0; i <= N; i++) {
            double probability = calculateProbability(N, i);
            
            if (probability >= P) {
                out.println(i);
                break;
            }
        }

        out.close();
    }
    
    // Calculate probability that at least one of the studied maps is selected
    // when 3 maps are shown, each player discards one, and system randomly selects
    // from remaining maps that no one picked
    public static double calculateProbability(int N, int studied) {
        // Total ways to choose 3 maps from N
        long totalWays = (long)N * (N-1) * (N-2) / 6;
        
        if (totalWays == 0) return 0.0;
        
        // Count favorable cases where at least one studied map appears in final game
        // Instead, calculate complement: probability that NO studied map is played
        // This happens when all 3 shown maps include 0 or 1 studied maps, and both players
        // discard the studied map (if present), and system picks from unstudied
        
        // Case 1: 0 studied maps shown
        // Choose 3 unstudied maps: C(N-studied, 3)
        long case1 = 0;
        int unstudied = N - studied;
        if (unstudied >= 3) {
            case1 = (long)unstudied * (unstudied-1) * (unstudied-2) / 6;
        }
        
        // Case 2: 1 studied map shown
        // Choose 1 studied and 2 unstudied: C(studied, 1) * C(unstudied, 2)
        // Both players must discard the studied map (probability 1/2 * 1/2 = 1/4)
        // System then picks from 2 unstudied maps, so probability to get unstudied = 1
        long case2 = 0;
        if (studied >= 1 && unstudied >= 2) {
            case2 = (long)studied * (unstudied * (unstudied-1) / 2);
            // Both players need to discard the studied map: each has 1/3 chance to pick it
            // But actually, each player randomly picks one of 3 maps to discard
            // So probability both discard the studied map = (1/3) * (1/3) = 1/9
            // Wait, let me reconsider...
            
            // Actually, with 1 studied map S and 2 unstudied maps U1, U2:
            // Each player randomly picks one of the 3 maps to discard
            // For no studied map to be played, both players must discard S
            // Probability player 1 discards S = 1/3
            // Probability player 2 discards S = 1/3
            // So probability = 1/9
            case2 = case2 * 1; // The system will pick from U1,U2 regardless, so probability of unstudied = 1
        }
        
        // Case 3: 2 studied maps shown
        // Choose 2 studied and 1 unstudied: C(studied, 2) * C(unstudied, 1)
        // For no studied map to be played, both players must discard both studied maps
        // But there are 2 studied maps and 1 unstudied map: S1, S2, U
        // Each player discards one map randomly
        // For no studied map to be played, both players must discard the same studied map
        // Then system picks from remaining 2 maps (1 studied, 1 unstudied)
        // Probability system picks unstudied = 1/2
        // But actually, we want probability that final map is unstudied
        // Let's enumerate:
        // Player1 discards S1, Player2 discards S1 -> system picks from {S2, U} -> prob unstudied = 1/2
        // Player1 discards S1, Player2 discards S2 -> system picks from {U} -> prob unstudied = 1
        // Player1 discards S1, Player2 discards U -> system picks from {S2} -> prob unstudied = 0
        // ... etc
        
        // Actually, let me reconsider the problem from scratch.
        // We want probability that the final game map is studied.
        // There are 3 maps shown: A, B, C
        // Each player independently picks one to discard
        // System picks randomly from maps not discarded by anyone
        
        // For a studied map to be played, it must be among the 3 shown, and not discarded by either player
        
        // Let's compute directly: probability that final map is studied
        double favorable = 0.0;
        
        // Iterate over all possible sets of 3 maps
        // For each set, compute probability that final map is studied
        
        // Instead of iterating over all combinations, use combinatorics
        
        // Case 0: 0 studied maps in the 3 shown
        // Probability = C(N-studied, 3) / C(N, 3)
        // Final map is unstudied (probability 0 of studied)
        
        // Case 1: 1 studied map in the 3 shown
        // Probability = C(studied, 1) * C(N-studied, 2) / C(N, 3)
        // Let the maps be S, U1, U2
        // Each player picks one of 3 maps to discard uniformly at random
        // For S to be played: both players must NOT discard S
        // Probability a player doesn't discard S = 2/3
        // Probability both don't discard S = (2/3)^2 = 4/9
        // If both don't discard S, then S is played (since the only maps are S, U1, U2, and if neither discards S, then at least S is not discarded)
        // Actually, if both don't discard S, they each discard one of U1, U2
        // So possible discards: (U1,U1), (U1,U2), (U2,U1), (U2,U2)
        // In all cases, S is not discarded, so S is played
        // So probability S is played = 4/9
        
        // Case 2: 2 studied maps in the 3 shown
        // Probability = C(studied, 2) * C(N-studied, 1) / C(N, 3)
        // Maps: S1, S2, U
        // For a studied map to be played, at least one of S1 or S2 must not be discarded by either player
        // Let's enumerate all 9 combinations of discards:
        // Player1 discards S1, Player2 discards S1 -> system picks from {S2, U} -> prob studied = 1/2
        // Player1 discards S1, Player2 discards S2 -> system picks from {U} -> prob studied = 0
        // Player1 discards S1, Player2 discards U -> system picks from {S2} -> prob studied = 1
        // Player1 discards S2, Player2 discards S1 -> system picks from {U} -> prob studied = 0
        // Player1 discards S2, Player2 discards S2 -> system picks from {S1, U} -> prob studied = 1/2
        // Player1 discards S2, Player2 discards U -> system picks from {S1} -> prob studied = 1
        // Player1 discards U, Player2 discards S1 -> system picks from {S2} -> prob studied = 1
        // Player1 discards U, Player2 discards S2 -> system picks from {S1} -> prob studied = 1
        // Player1 discards U, Player2 discards U -> system picks from {S1, S2} -> prob studied = 1
        // Total probability = (1/2 + 0 + 1 + 0 + 1/2 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1) / 9 = 7/9
        
        // Case 3: 3 studied maps in the 3 shown
        // Probability = C(studied, 3) / C(N, 3)
        // Maps: S1, S2, S3
        // For a studied map to be played: at least one of S1, S2, S3 is not discarded by either player
        // Since there are 3 maps and 2 discards, at least 1 map is not discarded
        // And since all maps are studied, probability = 1
        
        long case0 = 0;
        if (unstudied >= 3) {
            case0 = (long)unstudied * (unstudied-1) * (unstudied-2) / 6;
        }
        
        long case1 = 0;
        if (studied >= 1 && unstudied >= 2) {
            case1 = (long)studied * (unstudied * (unstudied-1) / 2);
        }
        
        long case2 = 0;
        if (studied >= 2 && unstudied >= 1) {
            case2 = (long)studied * (studied-1) / 2 * unstudied;
        }
        
        long case3 = 0;
        if (studied >= 3) {
            case3 = (long)studied * (studied-1) * (studied-2) / 6;
        }
        
        // Calculate total favorable probability
        favorable = case1 * 4.0/9.0 + case2 * 7.0/9.0 + case3 * 1.0;
        
        return favorable / totalWays;
    }

    static class FastScanner {
        InputStream dis;
        byte[] buffer = new byte[1 << 17];
        int pointer = 0;

        public FastScanner (String fileName) throws IOException {
            dis = new FileInputStream(fileName);
        }

        public FastScanner (InputStream is) throws IOException {
            dis = is;
        }

        int nextInt() throws IOException {
            int ret = 0;

            byte b;
            do {
                b = nextByte();
            } while (b <= ' ');
            boolean negative = false;
            if (b == '-') {
                negative = true;
                b = nextByte();
            }
            while (b >= '0' && b <= '9') {
                ret = 10 * ret + b - '0';
                b = nextByte();
            }

            return (negative) ? -ret : ret;
        }

        long nextLong() throws IOException {
            long ret = 0;

            byte b;
            do {
                b = nextByte();
            } while (b <= ' ');
            boolean negative = false;
            if (b == '-') {
                negative = true;
                b = nextByte();
            }
            while (b >= '0' && b <= '9') {
                ret = 10 * ret + b - '0';
                b = nextByte();
            }

            return (negative) ? -ret : ret;
        }

        byte nextByte() throws IOException {
            if (pointer == buffer.length) {
                dis.read(buffer, 0, buffer.length);
                pointer = 0;
            }
            return buffer[pointer++];
        }

        String nextString() throws IOException {
            StringBuilder ret = new StringBuilder();

            byte b;
            do {
                b = nextByte();
            } while (b <= ' ');
            while (b > ' ') {
                ret.appendCodePoint(b);
                b = nextByte();
            }

            return ret.toString();
        }

    }
}
